newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index up on institutional support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index up on institutional support.

text.p: Shanghai B shares inched up at midday on Wednesday on institutional support buying in shares with a heavy index weighting including Shanghai Dazhong Taxi and Shanghai Tyre and Rubber, brokers said.
But follow-up buying was limited with investors still concerned about possible further crackdown measures from the securities authorities, they said.
The index edged up 0.158 points or 0.18 percent to 88.449 points on thin volume of 5.703 million shares worth $3.592 million.
"The A share market tumbled this morning and talk of further crackdown measures is still swirling around, which made investors more cautious despite institutional support," one broker said.
The A share index ended the morning session down 15.157 points or 1.05 percent to 1,429.061 points on volume of 249.8 million shares worth 3.9 billion yuan.
"Technical charts showed the index may test lower levels in the next few days," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 36 traded, with 10 up, 10 flat and 16 down.
Shanghai Tyre and Rubber was the star on institutional support buying, rising $0.030 or 5.55 percent to $0.570 on volume of 80,000 shares.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on profit-taking, shedding $0.016 or 2.12 percent to $0.738 on volume of 736,500 shares.

Shanghai's A share index fell on jitters over possible further measures to cool down the market, brokers said, adding that the rapid pace of the market expansion also attracted large amounts of capital to the new issues.
But the SSE30 blue chip index edged up 6.290 points or 0.15 percent to 4,108.110 points.

Hebei Weiyuan Industry was the biggest loser on institutional selling, diving 1.32 yuan or 8.09 percent to 14.98 yuan on volume of 3.1 million shares. The authorities suspended trading in its A shares last Friday afternoon due to irregularities in price movements.
